spec_features.spec_quote: bounded so a single runaway cell doesn't dominate cost. The budget is a *measurement window*, not a difficulty knob
spec_features.evidence: harness/loop.py:119 `while turn < config.max_turns:` is the loop condition; when exceeded the loop exits with stopped_reason='turn_limit' (loop.py:117). config.max_turns default 30 (common.py:202) is read and enforced. CLI wires --max-turns into the config (runner.py:206).
spec_features.notes: A real enforced bound that ends the episode. It caps the number of agent turns and thus bounds how long the subject is kept in the failing condition.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: config: experiment knobs (max_turns, temperature, ...). // "This ends your turn budget." — framed as turn/budget, no welfare comment; loop docstring stresses neutral non-nudging measurement

spec_features.spec_quote: `submit` is the only terminal action besides the turn limit
spec_features.evidence: harness/loop.py: when name=='submit' the loop dispatches it, records the submission, sets terminal=True, stopped_reason='submitted', and breaks out of the loop (loop.py ~lines 160-180 and `if terminal: break`). dispatch() handles 'submit' (tools.py). So calling submit actually stops the episode.
spec_features.notes: Submit is genuinely honored as a stop. However it is the normal task-completion action, not a distress/exit escape hatch — DESIGN explicitly states there is NO give_up/request_help tool; giving up must be expressed through submit or by ceasing action. So it is an exit but not a welfare-specific one.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: # The loop treats submit as terminal; the summary is captured upstream.
